The goal of the recodeflow library is to enable the creation of a study 
dataset in an open, transparent, and reproducible manner. 

One of the first steps in any quantitative study is the selection and creation 
of variables that will be used to answer the research question. However, this 
process is not usually conducted in a transparent manner resulting in 
studies that are:

1. **Inefficient**: Previous work done by research teams are rarely 
   transferable to new studies, even if they use the same 
   variables.
2. **Non-reproducible**: The lack of transparency makes 
   it impossible for a published study to be reproduced without extensive help from the 
   original authors.
   If enough time has passed since publication, even the original authors may 
   not remember how the study variables were created. 

Predictive algorithm studies are especially susceptible to these problems. 
The large number of variables in these studies as well as the increasingly complex transformations 
done on them makes it impossible to not 
only reproduce but also score these algorithms on new data.

The recodeflow library solves these issues by: **1.** Encoding all the recoding 
rules in a set of CSV sheets that are transparent and machine actionable; and
**2.** Providing software to create a study dataset using the CSV sheets.

Although the library has accomplished its above mentioned goal there is still work to be done
to fix issues reported by its users. These include ones like users not knowing
why a function failure has taken place (not enough logging), the 
documentation not catering to different types of users (not using the divio 
style of documentation), the function having too many parameters (complex API)
etc.

This document contains the scope for the next version of the library that aims 
to address the above and other issues. Explore the scope for different parts 
of the library by clicking on one of links below.
